title: Language names in singular partitive
summary: When saying which language you speak or study, use singular partitive: Puhun suomea. — I speak Finnish. Opiskelen englantia. — I study English. Finnish language names use lower-case letters; speaking about a topic follows a different pattern.
objectives: Use singular partitive language names with the supplied speaking and studying verbs.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use singular partitive language names with the supplied speaking and studying verbs.
Keep language names lower-case in Finnish. Speaking a language and speaking about a topic are different constructions; only the language construction is practised here.
The verb forms are supplied. Do not infer that these verbs use one case for every possible meaning.
keyPoints: A language name uses singular partitive after speaking or studying in these familiar constructions.

steps: A language name uses singular partitive after speaking or studying in these familiar constructions.
Puhun means “I speak” and works as the verb. puhun comes from puhua: puhu- + -n.
suomea means “Finnish language” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Change final i in suomi to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -a: suomea.
A language name uses singular partitive after speaking or studying in these familiar constructions.
Puhun means “I speak” and works as the verb. puhun comes from puhua: puhu- + -n.
ruotsia means “Swedish language” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep ruotsi and add -a: ruotsi + a = ruotsia.
A language name uses singular partitive after speaking or studying in these familiar constructions.
Opiskelen means “I study” and works as the verb. opiskelen comes from opiskella: opiskele- + -n.
englantia means “English language” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep englanti and add -a: englanti + a = englantia.
A language name uses singular partitive after speaking or studying in these familiar constructions.
Opiskelen means “I study” and works as the verb. opiskelen comes from opiskella: opiskele- + -n.
saksaa means “German language” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep saksa and add -a: saksa + a = saksaa.

commonMistakes: Keep the lower-case initial in Finnish language names.
Do not use the dictionary form as the language object.
